title: Satellite-detected flood water
dateMeaning: Three-day observation composite ending on the selected date; the current-day product may be partial.

classes.label: Flood water detected
classes.interpretation: Satellite water detection outside the reference water and recurring-flood classes; confirm locally before operational decisions.

classes.label: Recurring flood water
classes.interpretation: Detected water in locations identified by the reference mask as recurring flooding.

classes.label: Surface water
classes.interpretation: Detected water in the reference surface-water class, including normal water bodies; not evidence of new flooding.

classes.label: Insufficient observations
classes.interpretation: The product cannot establish surface conditions here; commonly due to clouds or incomplete observations.

classes.label: No water detected / transparent
classes.interpretation: No water detected by this product; does not exclude narrow, urban, under-canopy, or short-lived flooding.

qualityNotes: An observation composite is not a forecast and is not a ground-confirmed incident report.
Gray pixels are unknown conditions, not dry land and not flooded land.
The nominal 250 m resolution cannot resolve many street-level floods, narrow channels, or small flooded areas.
Clouds, tree cover, building roofs, shadows, and the timing of satellite passes can hide flooding or cause classification errors.
Three-day compositing reduces cloud-shadow false positives but mixes observations from different days, so flood water may since have moved or receded.
NASA's current-day NRT tiles are updated as observations arrive; product dates indicate the composite endpoint and do not guarantee complete local coverage.
A successful transparent PNG response by itself is not evidence that a location was observed or that no flooding occurred.
The GIBS display is graphic imagery, not an authoritative vector flood boundary or an affected-population measurement.

verification.coverageFinding: Today's regional preview was predominantly gray insufficient observations. The bounding box also includes parts of neighboring countries and the sea. It cannot substantiate a Somalia-wide flooded-area total or city-specific flood absence.

alternative.status: Public PNG verified, but regional preview had a very large insufficient-observation footprint; not preferable to MODIS in this verification.

limits: An observation composite is not a forecast and is not a ground-confirmed incident report.
Gray pixels are unknown conditions, not dry land and not flooded land.
The nominal 250 m resolution cannot resolve many street-level floods, narrow channels, or small flooded areas.
Clouds, tree cover, building roofs, shadows, and the timing of satellite passes can hide flooding or cause classification errors.
Three-day compositing reduces cloud-shadow false positives but mixes observations from different days, so flood water may since have moved or receded.
NASA's current-day NRT tiles are updated as observations arrive; product dates indicate the composite endpoint and do not guarantee complete local coverage.
A successful transparent PNG response by itself is not evidence that a location was observed or that no flooding occurred.
The GIBS display is graphic imagery, not an authoritative vector flood boundary or an affected-population measurement.
The observed flood extent excludes normally flooded reference-water areas.
Use scene footprints and the exclusion mask to separate no detection from unknown coverage.
Satellite scenes are snapshots; water can move or recede after acquisition.
Radar works through cloud but may miss flood water in dense vegetation, urban areas, and areas of weak radar sensitivity.
A scene footprint is the observed image extent, not the flooded area.
Flooded-pixel totals returned with a footprint refer to the entire satellite scene and must not be assigned to a city.
